{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABf6PVqg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhJXXqI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 383, "title": "Consolidate speech recognition to Moonshine English Medium + Japanese Small Streaming; completely remove all other ASR implementations", "body": "## Goal

**Reduce the project to exactly two speech-recognition AI Node types:**

1. **Keep** `SpeechToTextMoonshineMediumEn` — Moonshine **English Medium Streaming (245M)**.
2. **Add** `SpeechToTextMoonshineSmallJa` (or a similarly clear new stable internal type) — official Moonshine **Japanese Small Streaming (123M)**.

**Completely remove the other four ASR model/Node implementations**, including their unused assets, loaders, controls, code paths, test fixtures, dev tooling, and current documentation. **Do not preserve graph JSON, import/export, Node type, model-cache, or runtime backward compatibility** for the removed ASR nodes.

This is intentional, user-directed **breaking cleanup**. The goal is a lean codebase with two **native streaming** ASR models, not an adapter framework or legacy migration.

### Motivation

The user has tested the existing models on a capable Mac and prioritizes **recognition quality first**, then responsiveness and stability. The current ReazonSpeech ja-en, Whisper tiny and Zipformer English were not good enough in actual dictation; Parakeet neither handles Japanese nor provides streaming in this integration. Moonshine English Medium has been the most promising English option so far. Japanese Small is a promising **new model to integrate and test**, **not yet proven to meet the user's quality bar**.

## Authoritative final ASR inventory

| Action | Internal Node type | Model | Language | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **KEEP** | `SpeechToTextMoonshineMediumEn` | Moonshine Medium Streaming (245M) | English only | Real `provisional` + `final` |
| **ADD** | `SpeechToTextMoonshineSmallJa` | Moonshine Small Streaming (123M), official Japanese checkpoint | Japanese only | Real `provisional` + `final` |
| **DELETE** | `SpeechToTextReazonSpeech` | ReazonSpeech ja-en | Japanese/English | Removed entirely |
| **DELETE** | `SpeechToTextWhisper` | Whisper tiny q8 | Configured ja/en | Removed entirely |
| **DELETE** | `SpeechToTextZipformerEn` | Streaming Zipformer English | English | Removed entirely |
| **DELETE** | `SpeechToTextParakeetV3` | Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 | Multilingual excluding Japanese | Removed entirely |

Delete **Silero VAD** and its cache/download/runtime only if no remaining feature uses it. Preserve unrelated dependency assets such as the **Kokoro Japanese/OpenJTalk frontend**, which is TTS, not ASR.

### User-visible names and model cards

- English Node primary label: **`Speech Recognition · EN / Streaming`**, secondary **`Moonshine Medium Streaming English`**.
- Japanese Node primary label: **`Speech Recognition · JA / Streaming`**, secondary **`Moonshine Small Streaming Japanese`**.
- Keep the existing AI icon + function-first presentation from #380. Settings show accurate **Model, Languages, Runtime**; both models are **language-specific**, not interchangeable via a language flag.
- Exactly **two ASR options** in Graph Editor / Add Node and **two ASR model cards** in Models. No ghost entries for removed variants.

## Required implementation work

### 1. Integrate Japanese Small as genuine browser-local streaming inference

- Use the **official Moonshine Japanese Small Streaming (123M)** checkpoint, not old Japanese Base/Tiny, an English model renamed Japanese, or an unrelated fine-tune. Confirm current published assets and the revision before pinning. Source: [Moonshine official model inventory](https://github.com/moonshine-ai/moonshine/blob/main/docs/models/available-models.md).
- Obtain all required deploy artifacts (e.g. ORT/ONNX weights, frontend, decoder, tokenizer, streaming config), review **model/runtime licenses**, source paths/URLs, exact sizes and cryptographic hashes. Pin all files in a new integrity-checked manifest following the project's `ModelAssetCache` conventions. Use normal model download/cache/verification/retry/abort; no model weights bundled with the extension, no cloud inference.
- Check whether the project's pinned `@moonshine-ai/moonshine-wasm` runtime supports **Japanese + `SmallStreaming`** for the actual pinned checkpoint. If not, upgrade/patch **one shared Moonshine runtime** with reviewed, checksum-pinned vendor build assets; do not fabricate outputs or silently fall back to English.
- Configure the transcriber with the **correct Japanese language / asset selection, Small Streaming architecture and tokenizer**. Upstream specifically warns that non-Latin languages may need a higher hallucination/too-many-tokens guard (`max_tokens_per_second = 13`); investigate, configure and test it if the active runtime exposes this option. See [official model documentation](https://github.com/moonshine-ai/moonshine/blob/main/docs/models/available-models.md) and [accuracy notes](https://github.com/moonshine-ai/moonshine/blob/main/docs/models/accuracy.md).
- Reuse the current Moonshine incremental streaming, Worker lifecycle, `OptionalAsrCore` typed ports and 30-second bounded buffering where appropriate. A **thin model-specific configuration** is preferable to duplicating the English engine or creating a universal ASR adapter. Make sure both languages actually emit authentic provisional/final transcript events, preserve Unicode Japanese text and correct IDs, and can Stop/drain/Cancel/restart independently.
- Keep the **existing English Medium** pinned checkpoint/quality/stream semantics intact (no forced re-download, model replacement or unrequested behavioral change). Consider factoring only truly identical Moonshine code into a small shared module.

### 2. Hard-delete the other ASR implementations from the current tree

Remove source/runtime **only when no remaining non-ASR consumers require it**:

- Registry, palette and default graphs: remove the four deleted type IDs from `extension/graph.js` `NODE_TYPES`, `ASR_TYPES`, `extension/graph-palette.js`, graph runtime dispatch, validator/port rules, graph templates/presets, model requirements, cache cards and default Graph Library entries. Make a deliberate **new default graph** using a retained Moonshine model and document its explicit language, rather than leaving any ReazonSpeech references.
- Delete now-unused ASR modules: Reazon/sherpa-onnx path and simulation/core, Whisper node/worker/config, Zipformer node/worker/config, Parakeet node/worker/segments, their manifests and model cache exports. Trim shared modules where a removed implementation was the only consumer; **retain** reused microphone/tab capture, transcription contracts, streaming output, Moonshine runtime and non-ASR infrastructure.
- Delete orphaned **Silero VAD** model and runtime if all its consumers are gone. Do not confuse unrelated embedded or TTS audio processing requirements with the old standalone Silero ASR cache asset.
- Purge removed dependencies, weight-free vendor bundles and scripts from preparation/build/CI/packaging: `scripts/prepare-*-assets.py`, `scripts/*assets.json`, optional ASR preparation manifest, `package.json` scripts/dependencies/lockfile, `scripts/build-extension.py`, `scripts/prepare-playground-assets.py`, GitHub Actions and vendor notices as appropriate. Keep only Moonshine-related optional-ASR assets and code; rename overly generic/obsolete “optional ASR” wrappers where doing so simplifies rather than complicates the architecture.
- Update **standalone Node Playground** too: remove the deleted four dedicated ASR test pages and all their links, leave independent browser test pages for **English Medium** and **Japanese Small**, maintain direct links/index and local/Pages deployment. This is part of the cleanup, not an exception to it.
- Remove current README, user-facing help, docs, fixtures and tests that refer to the four deleted choices as active. Do not preserve dead tests merely to check legacy compatibility. Historical Git commits/closed Issues remain in GitHub history; **“no traces” means no obsolete implementation paths/references in the active source tree and deliverables**, not rewriting published Git history.
- `Models` must contain exactly the two remaining ASR model entries, plus all unrelated model families and their necessary dependencies. Remove unused asset IDs/source notices and keep proper attribution for retained components.
- Review and update every current source-code reference to deleted Node IDs / filenames. A targeted search such as `rg 'SpeechToTextReazonSpeech|SpeechToTextWhisper|SpeechToTextZipformerEn|SpeechToTextParakeetV3|reazon|silero|whisper|zipformer|parakeet' extension web scripts tests docs .github package.json` should expose **no runtime dead paths or current active guidance**; treat intentional historical changelog/evidence references differently only if retaining them is necessary.

### 3. Intentionally break old graph compatibility, without compatibility scaffolding

- **No migration layer, aliases, legacy loaders, deprecation shims, retained Node types, conditional import/export rewrites or automatic substitution** for the four removed ASRs.
- Saved/imported/exported graphs containing those old types are **unsupported**. Fail with a clear, generic graph-validation / unsupported-type message and guide the user to recreate/reset the graph; do not silently map them to a Moonshine Node (different language/capabilities/ports). **No requirement to preserve or repair previously saved graphs**; user explicitly accepts breakage.
- Keep valid modern graph JSON import/export and Auto Save functional for the **two retained** ASR types and **all other unaffected Node types**. Schema/version may be changed as needed for the clean current implementation.
- Update any default/test/example graph to use one of the two remaining models with appropriate language. Do not load both unnecessarily or infer a language for mixed speech.

### 4. Test and acceptance

- [ ] Only Moonshine English Medium and Japanese Small appear in the ASR palette, graph metadata, runtime dispatch, Models and standalone model test index.
- [ ] Real Japanese Small loads **official pinned** model files with appropriate language + streaming architecture and produces correctly decoded Japanese **interim and final** text on realistic Japanese speech. Verify it does not silently drop Japanese content or terminate due to a token-rate guard appropriate only to English.
- [ ] Real English Medium retains existing streaming behavior and local output; verify both independent model initialization paths, Stop/tail drain, Cancel, restart, isolation, cancellation during loading, offline cache reuse, storage verification and bounded memory/backpressure.
- [ ] The in-page microphone, toolbar-launched graphs, browser tab audio, typed `provisional`/`final` ports and downstream formatting/translation/display/text insertion still work with the **retained models**.
- [ ] Automated browser tests cover both ASR models and test-page interactions, including index navigation and deployment-path resolution. Include **opt-in real model smoke tests with short, known Japanese and English speech fixtures**; mock tests alone do not establish recognition accuracy. Record observed latency and representative transcript quality but **do not make a manual visual approval or large weight download a default CI gate**.
- [ ] The four deleted ASR Node types, their manifests/Models cards/worker files/vendor runtimes/standalone pages and unused dependencies no longer exist in the active source tree or packaged extension and Pages artifact.
- [ ] No legacy graph import/export conversion or backward-compatibility paths remain; old graphs fail normal validation, and new or current supported graphs still round-trip.
- [ ] All surviving **non-ASR** AI Nodes (translation, text, TTS), Graph Library, model cache management and runtime functionality are unaffected.
- [ ] Update tests, docs, packaging and CI expectations so that the newly supported production set is the source of truth. Run relevant unit/browsers/extension tests and document any genuinely unrelated pre-existing failures.
- [ ] An implementation/evidence note clearly lists what was removed and verifies there are no dangling imports/unused bundled assets.

## Out of scope

- Adding Whisper large or another new ASR family, language auto-detection, a universal model registry, a comparison/ranking UI, or any additional model variants.
- Reintroducing old ASR code just to rescue saved graphs.
- Deleting unrelated models or rewriting historical Git commits.
